title: SRE weekly update - 2026-05-09
body:
Summary:
- Week of 2026-05-03 -> 2026-05-09. Short week for some folks (offsite), but we had a medium-severity incident that impacted a subset of hosted API traffic in us-west-2.
- Main focus: incident triage & postmortem, SLO health for token-generation endpoints, improving on-call handoff notes and runbook gaps.

Highlights / quick bullets:
- Incident on 2026-05-05 03:14 PDT (see Incident section) - ~18 minutes of elevated 5xxs for hosted/text-generation on us-west-2 due to NAT gateway SNAT exhaustion on a new autoscale group.
- p99 latency for text-generation increased to 820ms (target 750ms) for 2h during canary rollout of batching change on 2026-05-07 - rollback initiated by oncall.
- Error budget: hosted-api/text-gen consumed 3.2% of monthly error budget this week (SLO: 99.7% availability).
- On-call handoffs: implemented a short-form Handoff template that reduces ambiguity (see linked runbook).

Incidents:
1) Incident: us-west-2 hosted/text-gen partial outage (2026-05-05 03:14 - 03:32 PDT)
   - Impact: 18m window of ~2.1% requests returning 5xx (spike to 5xx-classes for a subset of routes). Some sustained increased latencies afterward until autoscale corrected. Affected customers: small percentage of prod traffic in us-west-2, no customer data loss.
   - Root cause (preliminary): new autoscale group linked to private subnet had insufficient NAT port capacity - SNAT exhaustion when many short-lived connections to external config service started during a deploy. Autoscaler created many instances quickly; each created transient left-over connections.
   - Detection: Pager triggered by 5xx count alert (alerts/SRE-1872).
   - Mitigation steps taken: rollback of recent infra change (reverted ASG config), manually increased NAT gateway capacity and temporarily switched some canary traffic to us-east-1. Restarted config service with connection pooling.
   - Follow-ups: (a) add SNAT capacity checks to deploy playbook (JIRA SRE-1878), (b) add synthetic test that simulates short-lived connection patterns pre-deploy, (c) update autoscale lifecycle hooks to warm connections and stagger scale-up.

2) Near-miss: p99 latency regression during batcher canary (2026-05-07)
   - We saw p99 spike to 820ms for ~2 hours after enabling continuous-batching tuning on a canary subset. Oncall rolled back the batcher tuning; p99 returned to normal. Action: add more rigorous perf tests for tail latency before canary. Related PR: infra#2142.

SLO & metrics snapshot:
- Hosted API - text-generation availability SLO: target 99.7% per-month. Current month to date: 99.62% (down from 99.66 last week) - error budget used ~3.2% (monthly budget 6%).
- p50/p95/p99 latency (text-gen, prod, all regions): p50 120ms, p95 310ms, p99 740ms (target p99 <= 750ms).
- On-call alert noise: ~12 actionable alerts this week (down from 18). Still seeing repeated noisy alert from node-exporter OOM metric in k8s-cluster-nonprod - ticketed to infra.

On-call handoffs / notes:
- Handoff template now required for all 8:00 and 20:00 shifts. Template fields: current-incidents, recent changes, outstanding action items, expected escalations, pager rotation. Saved in Confluence runbook.
- This week's handoff highlights: incoming oncall (Priya) flagged two config changes scheduled for Mon morning - recommended to delay until NAT fix deployed.
- Reminder: escalation path updated - second-level oncall must join within 10 minutes for any P2 or higher.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- SRE-1878: Add SNAT/capacity check to deploy pipeline + synthetic test for short-lived connection patterns. Owner: Mateo. ETA: 2026-05-16.
- infra#2142 follow-ups: Add tail-latency perf test for batcher tuning. Owner: Jordan. ETA: 2026-05-14.
- Runbook update: Add explicit autoscaler lifecycle hook guidance and handoff checklist. Owner: Ava. ETA: 2026-05-12.
- Alert tuning: suppress node-exporter OOM noise for nonprod clusters. Owner: Platform Eng. ETA: 2026-05-11.

Runbook / playbook notes:
- Added quick SNAT check (./scripts/check-snat.sh) to pre-deploy steps - temp manual step until pipeline automation done.
- Playbook step for urgent mitigation: if SNAT exhaustion suspected, route canary to alternate region and scale down new ASG.

Risks / blockers:
- We currently rely on cloud NAT gateway autoscaling limits that are not visible in the standard deploy dashboard. Need infra support to surface port exhaustion metrics.
- Rollouts of batcher tuning require a more robust canary harness (we only had basic traffic shaping).

Upcoming changes / planned work next week:
- Deploy automated SNAT capacity gating in CI (SRE + infra pairing).
- New canary harness for latency-sensitive tunings (batcher, kernel updates).
- SRE/Platform joint runbook session: 2026-05-12 10:00 PT (invite sent).

Notes to self / open questions:
- Should we default new autoscale groups to use connection-pooling-enabled AMI? pros/cons? (discuss with infra).
- Consider adding a short-lived connection synthetic to daily smoke tests (lightweight, runs in staging).

Attachments / links:
- Incident ticket: JIRA/SRE-1872
- Postmortem (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/2026-05-05+us-west-2+SNAT+exhaustion+postmortem
- PRs and perf graphs: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/production/text-gen-tail-latency

TL;DR: one medium incident due to SNAT exhaustion during a rapid autoscale + a canary-induced tail latency spike. Mitigations in place; follow-ups prioritized - key near-term work is automating pre-deploy SNAT checks and improving canary/perf tests for tail latency-sensitive changes.

-- Ava (SRE lead)
